newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh rebel peace envoy gunned down.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh rebel peace envoy gunned down.

text.p: Suspected tribal rebels have shot dead a peace envoy in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts, throwing negotiations to end a decades-old insurgency in the region into disarray, police said on Thursday.
They said Subinoy Chakma, Secretary General of Chittagong Hill Tracts National Coordination and Peace Council, was shot dead near his home at Rangamati hill town on Wednesday evening.
He was shot in the head, police said. They said they believed the killers were members of the hardline tribal insurgent group, called Shanti Bahini (peace force).
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday night ordered police to hunt down Chakma's killer.
Hill Tracts officials said the killing of Chakma, who belongs to the area's biggest tribe, might create distrust among local residents about the on-going peace process.
The Shanti Bahini has been fighting a bush war for autonomy of the 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, since 1973.
They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency.

The government and the Parbatya Chittagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political arm of the Shanti Bahini, held their latest peace meeting on Tuesday, when both sides reported progress towards finding a solution.
Both sides said they expected to be able to draw a draft peace formula in their next meeting scheduled for January 25.
Police said Chakma's killing was a violation of a ceasefire in the Hill Tracts, which was recently extended up to March 31.
